import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error

def interpolation_methods():
    # Create time series with sine wave pattern
    np.random.seed(42)
    t = np.arange(0, 50, 1)
    original = np.sin(0.3 * t) + 0.1 * np.random.randn(50)
    
    # Introduce missing values
    df = pd.DataFrame({'value': original}, index=pd.Index(t, name='time'))
    missing_idx = [5, 6, 7, 15, 16, 25, 26, 27, 28, 35, 36, 45]
    df.loc[missing_idx, 'value'] = np.nan
    
    print(f"Missing values: {df['value'].isnull().sum()}")
    
    # Linear interpolation
    df_linear = df.interpolate(method='linear')
    
    # Polynomial interpolation
    df_poly = df.interpolate(method='polynomial', order=2)
    
    # Spline interpolation
    df_spline = df.interpolate(method='spline', order=3)
    
    # Compare MSE on missing indices
    methods = {
        'Linear': df_linear,
        'Polynomial': df_poly,
        'Spline': df_spline
    }
    
    print("\nInterpolation MSE comparison:")
    for name, df_interp in methods.items():
        mse = mean_squared_error(
            original[missing_idx],
            df_interp.loc[missing_idx, 'value']
        )
        print(f"{name:12s}: MSE = {mse:.6f}")
    
    print("\nSample values at missing positions:")
    comparison = pd.DataFrame({
        'Original': original[missing_idx],
        'Linear': df_linear.loc[missing_idx, 'value'].values,
        'Polynomial': df_poly.loc[missing_idx, 'value'].values,
        'Spline': df_spline.loc[missing_idx, 'value'].values
    })
    print(comparison.round(4))

interpolation_methods()
